cues: White translucent box cut off by the top edge at the firewall, on the driver side of an RHD Tata diesel (image left = car right). Cap is not visible. The cooling system has its own pressure cap on the radiator (bottom), which fits a brake/clutch master-cylinder reservoir here better than a coolant tank. The box covers the visible part.

Dark shot. Cream translucent reservoir with a moulded flange seam sits on a round metal master-cylinder boss; the cap is not visible. The old box also took in the metal boss below (y 0.35-0.43), so the new box is tightened to the plastic body.

Blue cap embossed 'WASHER ONLY' with a windshield+spray icon, on a long filler neck at the front corner beside the airbox (Hyundai/Kia). The tank body is hidden below. The box covers the cap and neck, which is correct for washer.

Small round cream reservoir with a black screw cap, a mounting flange with a bolt and a small hose at the top: the remote PS reservoir of a Chrysler 3.6 minivan. Coolant on this car is filled through the separate metal 'DO NOT OPEN HOT' pressure cap just below it. The yellow cap below is the washer (windshield icon). The box ends at the washer cap top (y 0.635), about right; the mask may need trimming.

The same Chrysler 3.6 PS reservoir (cylindrical cream body, moulded MAX/MIN, mounting flange), clipped at the left edge. The old box merged it with the washer neck and yellow windshield-icon cap below (y 0.75-0.99), which is a separate washer_fluid_reservoir. The new box is tight on the PS reservoir only.

Metal pressure cap embossed 'DO NOT OPEN HOT' on a filler neck at the front radiator support, with no translucent tank under it (Chrysler 3.6 minivan; the PS reservoir and yellow washer cap are separate at its left). The object is the cap itself, so the cap box is complete.

Out-of-focus white tank at the top edge with a printed sticker and a clamped outlet hose at its bottom. Hybrid bay (orange HV cable, Hitachi MAF), so likely the engine or inverter coolant tank. No cap visible. The old box was shifted right into the dark area (x 0.33-0.41) and cut off the tank's left part.

Black cap embossed 'COOLANT' on a translucent white tank at the front-left corner, with an overflow hose. The large Hyundai/Kia radiator pressure cap is separate at the centre. Part of the tank body is visible right of the cap. The old box took in the hose above and the hood-latch bracket (x 0.18-0.25), so the new box is tight on the cap and visible body.

underbody view; large translucent tank low in the front corner next to the radiator lower tank and its white drain petcock; no cap, MIN/MAX or fluid colour visible. Low front-corner mounting fits the washer bottle (same vehicle's washer neck runs down to the corner, coolant bottle sits high) - undecidable from pixels, identity is a best guess

metal radiator-type pressure cap with red warning label on a translucent tank with an info sticker = pressurised coolant tank (hybrid PCU/inverter coolant reservoir on this Honda hybrid, orange HV cables); brake reservoirs never use pressure caps. The real brake reservoir (black cap, translucent) is just behind it at ~[0.715, 0.245, 0.77, 0.335]. Tank body visible down to ~0.435 but box stops at 0.41
